program.name: Phase 2 Square Ordering
program.description: Production Square integration and a customer ordering page: Square Catalog as the menu source of truth, orders with participant-assigned class seats and atomic seat holding, Square-hosted checkout, real webhook signature verification and fulfillment, and database-level reservation capacity enforcement.
program.revisionNote: Replanned after converge returned requires-replan (2 blockers, 8 majors, critic gpt-5.6-terra). See the Revision history section of the program document.

technology.catalogStrategy: Postgres cache, scheduled refresh + catalog.version.updated invalidation
technology.cartStorage: Signed HTTP-only cookie, amounts recomputed server-side
technology.totals: Square computes the authoritative order total including tax
technology.coreComposition: Injected ports (SeatHolder) rather than core-to-core imports
technology.mutationSurface: Next.js Server Actions (first use in this codebase)
technology.notificationUrl: Per-stage secret with a post-deploy assertion against the Function URL

successCriteria.description: The ordering page lists cafe items sourced from the Square Catalog cache, with name, description, and price.
The ordering page lists published class occurrences with start time, price, and remaining seats.
A signed-in customer can add cafe items and a class seat to a cart and see a correct recomputed total.
Submitting a cart with a tampered price or amount is rejected; the order is created from server-side amounts only.
Checkout redirects to a Square-hosted payment page for the created order.
A signed payment webhook moves its matching order to PAID and writes exactly one payment_records row.
A paid order containing a class seat confirms its reservation; the seat is no longer offered.
Two concurrent holds on a one-seat occurrence yield exactly one held seat, and after payment exactly one confirmed reservation.
An expired hold releases its seat and returns it to the available count.
Webhook signature verification implements Square's notification-URL-plus-body scheme and rejects a forged signature.
The Square webhook Function URL is publicly reachable and rejects unsigned requests.
Catalog sync runs on schedule and on catalog.version.updated, upserting new items and tombstoning removed ones.
Replaying the same payment webhook, or resuming it after a mid-fulfillment crash, produces exactly one payment record and one fulfillment.
Server Actions reject unauthenticated callers through the shared authorize predicate.
Playwright covers browse to participant selection to cart to checkout redirect against a stubbed Square client.
docs/environment.md documents every new secret and the sandbox/production credential split.
Each class seat is assigned to a named household member, and the reservation records that participant.
A participant from another household is rejected server-side.
Order creation and seat holding are atomic: neither a seatless paid order nor an orderless hold can result.
A sandbox payment completed end to end delivers a signed webhook that fulfills its order.

packages.name: square-client
packages.description: NEW. Production implementation of the SquareClient interface wrapping the Square SDK: catalog reads, payment links, payment retrieval, refunds, and Square's real webhook signature verification. The only workspace member depending on the Square SDK.

packages.name: catalog-core
packages.description: NEW. Catalog cache sync and read paths: cafe items from the Square cache plus published offerings joined to upcoming occurrences with remaining seat counts.

packages.name: contracts
packages.description: Adds catalog, cart, and order types; the participant-carrying occurrence cart line; the SeatHolder port; widens SquareClient.createCheckout off its reservationId assumption and adds notificationUrl to signature verification.

packages.name: database
packages.description: Adds orders, order_line_items, and catalog_items tables, plus the reservations capacity trigger and seat_count column deferred in Phase 1.

packages.name: commerce-core
packages.description: Order lifecycle, server-side price resolution, atomic seat holding through the injected SeatHolder port, and the real startCheckout replacing the Phase 1 stub.

packages.name: reservation-core
packages.description: Real holdReservation, confirmReservation, and cancelReservation with database-level capacity enforcement, a transaction-accepting signature, and the hold-expiry sweep.

packages.name: customer-core
packages.description: Consumed unchanged; listHouseholdMembers supplies the participant picker.

packages.name: web
packages.description: The ordering page, cart with participant selection, checkout action, the server-only composition root, the order status page, and the first Server Actions in the codebase.

packages.name: ui
packages.description: Presentational primitives for catalog items, participant selection, cart lines, and order review.

packages.name: auth
packages.description: Consumed unchanged; the Server Action wrapper calls its existing authorize predicate rather than reading tokens directly.

packages.name: square-webhook
packages.description: Real signature verification at the HTTP entry point and retry-safe order and reservation fulfillment in the consumer.

packages.name: scheduled-task-worker
packages.description: Gains the catalog refresh task key and the reservation hold-expiry sweep.

packages.name: infra
packages.description: Square secrets per stage, the notification-URL secret and its post-deploy assertion, catalog and expiry schedules, the Function URL auth switch to public, and a signature-failure alarm.

catalog-core: catalog cache sync and read paths
commerce-core: order lifecycle, seat holding, and real startCheckout

Room and open-play booking; rooms remain display-only
